roster_ideas.title: Trade lead: a running back for a tight end, with Sam
roster_ideas.text: You have seven running backs and one tight end (the big guy who blocks and catches). That tight end, Kyle Pitts Sr., scored 1.5 this week. Sam just lost De'Von Achane for the season, per FantasyPros' injury desk, and she has two tight ends that FantasyPros' expert consensus ranks 5th (Sam LaPorta) and 7th (Dalton Kincaid). One of your spare backs, like D'Andre Swift (ranked 12th and on your bench), for Kincaid is worth floating. Treat it as an opener, not a sure thing.

roster_ideas.title: Trade lead: a spare back for a receiver, with Maya
roster_ideas.text: Seven running backs, four wide receivers: your bench is basically a running-back parking lot. Maya has it the other way around, with seven receivers and three backs, and her bench includes Tetairoa McMillan, whom FantasyPros' expert consensus ranks 19th at wide receiver. Swapping a back like Cam Skattebo (ranked 18th at running back) for a receiver like that would give you more options at WR and flex (the wild-card spot). It's an idea to explore, not a guarantee.

roster_ideas.title: Claim Tyler Shough for the QB spot
roster_ideas.text: Your quarterbacks scored 3.76 (Drake Maye) and 13.64 (Bryce Young) this week. Tyler Shough is a free agent: nobody in the league owns him, per FantasyPros' ownership numbers. FantasyPros' expert consensus ranks him 12th among quarterbacks for the rest of the season, right behind Maye (11th) and well ahead of Young (17th), so he's at least a better Plan B than Young, and its news desk says he threw four touchdowns this week. Alec Pierce is the obvious cut: FantasyPros' injury desk lists him on IR with a foot injury.

advice_cards.title: Zay Flowers is healthy and stuck on IR
advice_cards.text: Zay Flowers scored 15.4 this week from your IR spot (the injured-reserve parking space), and points there don't count. FantasyPros' news desk says he looked healthy after missing Week 2 with a hamstring issue, and its expert consensus ranks him 9th among wide receivers for the rest of the season. Get him back into your lineup before Week 4.

advice_cards.title: Brock Bowers is back. Start him.
advice_cards.text: Brock Bowers scored 27.6 on your bench this week while Dalton Schultz scored 6 at tight end. FantasyPros' news desk says this was Bowers' season debut and calls him a high-end TE1 (a top-tier tight end) going forward. FantasyPros' expert consensus ranks him 1st among tight ends for the rest of the season, and Schultz 16th.

roster_ideas.title: Backup plan for Bijan: Brian Robinson Jr.
roster_ideas.text: You only have three running backs, and none of them is on the bench. Brian Robinson Jr. plays behind Bijan Robinson in Atlanta, which makes him Bijan's handcuff (the backup who takes over if the starter gets hurt). Nobody in the league owns him, per FantasyPros' ownership numbers. FantasyPros' expert consensus ranks him 54th among running backs, so he's insurance, not a starter. One of your seven wide receivers could make room.

roster_ideas.title: Trade lead: spare receivers for a running back, with Amie
roster_ideas.text: You carry seven wide receivers and only three running backs, so if one back gets hurt, nobody's waiting behind him. On your bench, FantasyPros' expert consensus ranks Tetairoa McMillan 19th at wide receiver, Mike Evans 25th and Jalen Coker 26th. Amie has seven running backs and only four receivers, including Cam Skattebo (ranked 18th at running back). A receiver for a back would even out both rosters. It's a conversation starter, not a verdict.

advice_cards.title: A.J. Brown is taking up a bench spot
advice_cards.text: FantasyPros' injury desk lists A.J. Brown on injured reserve through Week 4, and he's sitting on your bench. If ESPN also shows him as IR, moving him to your IR slot frees a bench spot for a pickup, and you don't lose him.

roster_ideas.title: Achane is out for the year. Claim Ollie Gordon II.
roster_ideas.text: Sorry. FantasyPros' injury desk reports that De'Von Achane tore his ACL against the Chiefs and will miss the rest of the season. Ollie Gordon II is the Miami running back most likely to take over. FantasyPros calls him a borderline RB2 for now (a decent second running back) and nobody in the league owns him, per FantasyPros' ownership numbers. Jaylen Wright is also a free agent and should get some carries once he's healthy.

roster_ideas.title: Trade lead: a tight end for a running back, with Amie
roster_ideas.text: With Achane out for the season, your running backs are Breece Hall, Bhayshul Tuten and TreVeyon Henderson, and FantasyPros' expert consensus has none of them in its top 15 for the rest of the year. You do have two good tight ends (the big guys who block and catch), though: FantasyPros ranks Sam LaPorta 5th and Dalton Kincaid 7th. Amie is the mirror image, with seven running backs (D'Andre Swift, ranked 12th, sits on her bench) and just one tight end, Kyle Pitts Sr., who scored 1.5 this week. Kincaid for one of her backs is worth asking about. It's a starting point, not a verdict.

advice_cards.title: Puka and Jefferson: hold, don't fold
advice_cards.text: Your two star receivers both sat out, but FantasyPros' news desk sounds hopeful about both. The Rams' head coach is "hopeful" Puka Nacua plays in Week 4, and Justin Jefferson's ankle injury isn't expected to be long-term, so he could play against the Dolphins. Keep both. Check back as practice reports come in this week.
